overview.headline: Lincoln Proclamation shifts Civil War to fight for freedom

keyPoints.point: Lincoln proclamation declared enslaved people in rebellious areas free from January 1, 1863 onward
keyPoints.quote: President Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863

keyPoints.point: Ending slavery was not an initial war goal although slavery conflicts helped cause the war
keyPoints.quote: Even though sectional conflicts over slavery had been a major cause of the war, ending slavery was not a goal of the war.

keyPoints.point: As military measure proclamation applied only to seceded states and left loyal border states untouched
keyPoints.quote: It applied only to states that had seceded from the Union, leaving slavery untouched in the loyal border states.

keyPoints.point: Proclamation opened Union Army and Navy to Black men who fought for Union and freedom
keyPoints.quote: By the end of the war, almost 200,000 Black soldiers and sailors had fought for the Union and freedom.

keyTerms.gloss: Lincoln order declaring freedom for enslaved people in rebellious areas
keyTerms.quote: President Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863

keyTerms.gloss: withdrawal of Southern states from the Union that North fought to prevent
keyTerms.quote: Initially, the Civil War between North and South was fought by the North to prevent the secession of the Southern states and preserve the Union.

keyTerms.gloss: Lincoln warning that enslaved people in rebellion states would be declared free
keyTerms.quote: when President Lincoln issued his Preliminary Emancipation Proclamation

keyTerms.gloss: loyal states where slavery remained untouched by the proclamation
keyTerms.quote: It applied only to states that had seceded from the Union, leaving slavery untouched in the loyal border states.

keyTerms.gloss: military forces that accepted Black men enabling liberated to become liberators
keyTerms.quote: Moreover, the Proclamation announced the acceptance of Black men into the Union Army and Navy, enabling the liberated to become liberators.
